answer: Inter-Handoff Interval Floor. Each agent identity must leave a minimum gap between its request handoffs, and that gap widens like a canyon after any burst. Enforcement: a sliding window measures inter-arrival spacing; a gale of parallel requests from one identity collapses the allowed rate to a trickle for a cooldown period. A comet-like fast burst is thus self-defeating, since the floor resets on every premature call. Cost to attacker: real wall-clock time per identity, so N sybils need N idle waits, making mass identity creation linearly expensive in latency rather than cheap in capital.
